issues.title: Logger uses direct logging.getLogger initialization
issues.description: The rule requires logger instances to be created using the pattern `logger: "logging.Logger" = get_logger("module_name")` from prefect.logging, but the code uses the direct `logging.getLogger(__name__)` pattern instead.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
# Logger for SDK fetcher operations
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
issues.rule_name: Logger Instances Must Follow Standard Initialization Pattern

issues.title: Incorrect deployment filtering breaks full-name matching
issues.description: The deployment filtering logic checks `dep.name not in deployment_names` instead of checking `full_name not in deployment_names`. This causes the filter to incorrectly evaluate when users specify deployment names in 'flow-name/deployment-name' format. When a user provides a full deployment name like 'my-flow/production', the code checks if 'production' (the short name) is in the list containing 'my-flow/production', which fails, causing the deployment to enter the fallback matching logic unnecessarily. This breaks the fast-path check and could lead to incorrect filtering behavior where deployments are included or excluded inappropriately.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
# If filtering by deployment name, check the full name matches
        full_name = f"{flow_name}/{dep.name}"
        if deployment_names and dep.name not in deployment_names:
            # Only include if the full name matches (filter was by name parts)
            # Skip if user specified full names and this doesn't match
            found_match = False

issues.title: Missing type validation for work pool job variables schema
issues.description: The code removes the `isinstance(variables, dict)` type check before assigning `base_job_template["variables"]` to `job_vars_schema`. The `job_vars_schema` variable is typed as `dict[str, Any]` and is expected to be a dictionary throughout the SDK generation process. If `base_job_template["variables"]` contains a non-dict value (like a list, string, or other type due to malformed work pool configuration), this will cause type inconsistencies that could lead to runtime errors in downstream code that expects a dict, such as the template renderer or SDK generator that processes the schema.

issues.title: Removed strict zip validation enables silent data corruption
issues.description: The code removes `strict=True` from the `zip(pool_names_list, results)` call in the work pool parallel fetching logic. The strict parameter ensures that both iterables have the same length and raises a ValueError if they don't match. Without it, if there's a mismatch between the number of work pool names and the results from `asyncio.gather()` (which should never happen in correct code but could occur due to bugs in the async gather logic or unexpected exceptions), the zip will silently truncate to the shorter sequence. This means some work pool results could be dropped or mismatched with the wrong names, leading to incorrect work pool metadata in the generated SDK without any warning or error.

structured_output.summary:
The PR adds two docs pages for the beta `prefect sdk generate` command (a how-to guide and a CLI reference page), registers them in docs.json, and makes three small edits to `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py`. The docs are mostly accurate: the CLI flags and the `with_options()`/`with_infra()` parameters match `cli/sdk.py` and `templates/sdk.py.jinja`. The fetcher edits are not safe to merge. The deployment-name filter change silently drops the ambiguous-short-name warning. I confirmed this by running the tests: `tests/_sdk/test_fetcher.py::test_fetch_sdk_data_ambiguous_short_name_warning` passes on the base commit (34/34 in that file) and fails on the head commit (326 passed, 1 failed across `tests/_sdk/`). The other fetcher edits (a logger inserted mid-import-block, an unexplained removal of `strict=True`, and removal of a dict type guard) add lint errors and loosen defensive checks without a stated reason.

The async example in the how-to guide also has a real bug. `PrefectFlowRunFuture.result()` is synchronous, so `await future.result()` on line 132 raises a TypeError when copied. The async counterpart is `aresult()`. Because the PR is docs plus code with a red test, I recommend requesting changes rather than merging as-is.
structured_output.verdictRationale: A previously passing test now fails because of the `dep.name not in deployment_names` change, an unrelated fetcher edit the PR description never mentions. The docs' async example is also broken when copied. Both fixes are small, and the docs content is otherwise accurate, so this should be a quick revision rather than a rework.

architecture.overview:
`prefect sdk generate` is a beta CLI command in `src/prefect/cli/sdk.py`. It calls `generate_sdk` in `src/prefect/_sdk/generator.py`, which uses `fetch_sdk_data` in `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py` to pull flows, deployments, and work pools from the Prefect API. The fetcher applies the `--flow` and `--deployment` filters and builds `SDKData` models from `src/prefect/_sdk/models.py`. The renderer then fills `src/prefect/_sdk/templates/sdk.py.jinja` to produce a typed Python module with `deployments.from_name(...)`, `run()`, `run_async()`, `with_options()`, and `with_infra()`.

This PR does not change the generator or the template. It adds user documentation for that pipeline (a how-to page and a CLI reference page, both registered in `docs/docs.json`) and touches the fetcher in three places. The most important of these is the deployment-name filter, which decides which deployments end up in the generated SDK and whether ambiguity warnings are emitted.
steps: Entry point: the `prefect sdk generate` Typer command in `src/prefect/cli/sdk.py` takes `--output`, `--flow`, and `--deployment`, and passes the filters to `generate_sdk`.

Fetch stage: `fetch_sdk_data` in `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py` checks authentication, builds `FlowFilter` and `DeploymentFilter` from the filters, fetches deployments, then fetches flow names and work pools in parallel. The PR adds a debug log before the auth check and changes the work pool and deployment-name matching logic.

Filter stage: deployment matching is the sensitive part. Short names (`production`) match any flow and trigger the ambiguity warning. Full names (`flow/production`) must match exactly. The PR changes the guard that gates this loop, which determines whether short-name matches are recorded.
Render stage: `SDKData` is turned into a Python module by the generator and `sdk.py.jinja`. The PR does not touch this stage, and the option lists in the docs match the template signatures.

Docs: the how-to page `docs/v3/advanced/generate-custom-sdk.mdx` documents the same flow for users, and `docs/v3/api-ref/cli/sdk.mdx` is the reference page. docs.json now places the how-to under a new Deployments group in the Advanced tab.

findings.title: Deployment name filter change drops the ambiguous short-name warning
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py`, inside `fetch_sdk_data`, revert the guard at about line 397 from `if deployment_names and dep.name not in deployment_names:` back to `if deployment_names and full_name not in deployment_names:`. This change breaks the short-name ambiguity warning, which `tests/_sdk/test_fetcher.py::TestFetchSDKData::test_fetch_sdk_data_ambiguous_short_name_warning` covers. Keep the full-name matching behavior that the existing loop already implements. Then run `pytest tests/_sdk/` and confirm it passes.

findings.title: Async example awaits a synchronous result() call
findings.fixPrompt: In `docs/v3/advanced/generate-custom-sdk.mdx`, the async example in the "Async usage" section (line 132) uses `await future.result()`. `PrefectFlowRunFuture.result()` is synchronous, so the await raises a TypeError. Change it to `await future.aresult()`, which is the async method on the same class in `src/prefect/futures.py`. Keep the rest of the example unchanged.

findings.title: Logger inserted between import blocks causes four ruff E402 errors
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py`, the module-level `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` (lines 19-20) sits between imports, which causes ruff E402 errors on the `from prefect...` imports after it. Move the logger assignment to after the last import (after the `if TYPE_CHECKING:` block), and keep all imports grouped at the top. Then run `ruff check src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py` and confirm it is clean.

findings.title: Removed strict=True from zip() without explanation
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py`, `_fetch_work_pools_parallel` (line 220) iterates `zip(pool_names_list, results)`. Restore `strict=True` so a length mismatch raises rather than silently truncating. The repo already uses `strict=True` elsewhere, so this matches existing style.

findings.title: Dict type guard removed from work pool job variables
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py`, `_fetch_work_pool` (lines 179-182) now assigns `job_vars_schema = base_job_template["variables"]` without checking its type. Restore the `isinstance(variables, dict)` guard, or add a comment explaining why the API guarantees a dict. Keep the `WorkPoolInfo` construction unchanged.

findings.title: Docs option lists match the generator and CLI
findings.body: The option names and descriptions in both docs pages match the source. `--output`, `--flow`, and `--deployment` appear in `src/prefect/cli/sdk.py`, and the `with_options()` parameters (`tags`, `idempotency_key`, `work_queue_name`, `as_subflow`, `scheduled_time`, `flow_run_name`) match `templates/sdk.py.jinja`. The `flow-name/deployment-name` guidance also matches the fetcher's full-name matching. The CLI reference page follows the same generated format as the other pages in `docs/v3/api-ref/cli/`, and `docs.json` parses as valid JSON.

findings.title: Full-name deployment filter has test coverage
findings.body: The full-name filter (`--deployment my-flow/production`) is exercised by a test near `tests/_sdk/test_fetcher.py:424` and passes on both base and head. The short-name ambiguity test is the one that catches the regression above, which is useful signal that the existing suite protects this behavior.
